findings.summary: On Athena's own repository the doc in the working copy can drift from the prompts compiled into the running binary.
findings.evidence: The frames are compiled in with include_str! (lib.rs:35-65), and the plan keeps docs/agent-reference.md out of BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS. An agent therefore reads the doc as it stands at the job's base commit, while its prompts come from whichever binary is running. A later prompt edit and a doc edit can go out of step, and no test pairs them. Fix: Add one sentence to the doc header saying it describes the prompts of the same commit and may lag a running binary. Alternatively, have the new test compare the doc's section headings with the five role ids so that renaming a role breaks the test.

findings.summary: The pointer line costs tokens in every set on every repository, but the file it names exists in only one.
findings.evidence: The plan adds the line 'Optional depth: if docs/agent-reference.md exists in the working copy, read it for ...; every rule you must follow is stated here.' to all five common frames. That is about 120-150 bytes, or roughly 40-50 tokens per set (an estimate), and it is spent on every repository. On any repository other than Athena's own, the file is never there. Fix: Keep the line as short as possible, for example 'Optional: docs/agent-reference.md, if present, explains these rules.' State its cost in the CHANGELOG token table. That way the user can weigh the cost when answering the open question about compiling the doc in.

findings.summary: The fixture margin is about 45 tokens, which is thin enough that the forced edit to run_pin_tests.rs is a likely outcome, not an edge case.
findings.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs:1607-1618 asserts that the contract plus two verifier frames exceed the Verifier budget. At the target sizes that sum is about 1145 against a budget of about 1100, both estimates. If the verifier frame ends up about 130 bytes under its target, the assertion fails. Fix: Keep the plan's fallback, which deletes only the assertion and keeps the rendered-row check. In the final report, state which way it went and the measured sum and budget, so the verifier can match the scope note against the diff.

summary: I checked the round-4 plan against the snapshot using Read and Grep. I ran nothing. The things the plan relies on exist and say what the plan claims. The budget values are at lib.rs:174-180, the exact length check `len() == 977` is at lib.rs:369, the frame size bound `< 900` is at lib.rs:406, and the fixture assertion `assert_eq!(left, 0)` is at run_pin_tests.rs:1618, with the literal `of 2000 tokens` at line 1625. The sets that every_role_set_is_within_its_budget composes are at budgets.rs:339-393. The planner set is the contract plus the planner frame, and the critic set is the contract plus the critic frame. The severity lines are at critic.md:12-13 and verifier.md:10, and the `mirrors` and xtask `policy` test targets exist. I grepped for code that reads the frame text or the prompt files. Apart from wording tests the plan already lists, every reader either composes the text or uses the file path only (briefs.rs:1584-1616, verify.rs:3103-3107, the cap-change and cap-study include_str! calls, policy.rs:943-945). The plan's budget arithmetic holds as an estimate. With the target sizes, the largest verifier-side set is the study verifier at about 977 tokens, which gives a budget of 1100 under the 90% rule. The largest producer-side set is about 927, which gives 1050. The fixture's two-frame sum, about 1145, stays above 1100, and the plan has a scoped fallback if it does not. The padded set in an_over_budget_role_set_fails stays over budget. The remaining questions are design choices the plan already puts to the user: the optional doc and the unchanged Contract and Reader budgets. Athena's two scope findings are weighed. Both edits are forced by tests and the plan says it will report them. I found no blocker or major finding. Three minor points follow.
